answer: Decaying referral chains. Each new identity must be introduced by an existing one, and a fraction of the introducer's standing transfers to the newcomer. Standing decays toward a meadow-wide baseline unless the newcomer completes independent, randomly assigned tasks whose difficulty scales with chain depth. Clones therefore inherit a juniper-thin balance that shrinks at each hop, while the introducer loses standing capacity. An attacker must fund real task work per identity until the chain reaches its nadir, making each marginal clone cost more than its expected yield.
